## 1\. A model-wide upper bound on storage lifetime

Let \(\Lambda\) contain \(n\) finite-dimensional sites and let its complete nominal generator be

\[
\mathcal L_0=\sum_X\mathcal L_X,
\qquad
\|\mathcal L_0\|_\diamond\leq Jn,
\]

where \(J\geq1\) is a constant independent of system size. Bounded-range, bounded-density generators with uniformly bounded local superoperator strengths satisfy such an estimate.

Choose any \(0<\epsilon\leq1\)\. Consider the particular admissible perturbation

\[
\mathcal E=
\eta\sum_{v\in\Lambda}(\mathcal T_v-\mathrm{id}),
\qquad
\eta=\frac{\epsilon}{2},
\]

where \(\mathcal T_v\) completely depolarizes the entire on-site Hilbert space, including any controller or ancillary registers.

Because

\[
\|\eta(\mathcal T_v-\mathrm{id})\|_\diamond
\leq2\eta=\epsilon,
\]

this perturbation satisfies the required local budget. The total generator \(\mathcal K=\mathcal L_0+\mathcal E\) is physical GKLS.

### Proposition

For every encoding channel \(\mathcal A\), every decoding channel \(\mathcal B\), and every integer \(k\geq1\), define

\[
\tau=\frac1{2Jn},
\qquad
p_n=(1-e^{-\eta\tau})^n.
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{
\left\|
\mathcal B e^{k\tau\mathcal K}\mathcal A
-\mathrm{id}_{2}
\right\|_\diamond
\geq
1-e^{-kp_n/2}.
}
\]

The conclusion holds regardless of the encoded qubit's protection mechanism, the internal controllers, Hamiltonian evolution, powered resets, or decoding strategy.

### Proof

The depolarization terms admit an exact unraveling into \(n\) independent Poisson clocks, each firing at rate \(\eta\)\. Between depolarization events, the system evolves under the complete nominal semigroup \(e^{s\mathcal L_0}\)\.

Consider an interval of length \(\tau\)\. Let \(G\) be the event that every site experiences at least one complete depolarization during that interval. Independence of the clocks gives

\[
\Pr(G)=(1-e^{-\eta\tau})^n=p_n.
\]
